speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what is the justification for treating essential occupiers of HDB flats similar to HDB owners with respect to having to fulfil the minimum occupation period for purchase of private property, while treating such essential occupiers as non-owners for liability for Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider harmonising the treatment of essential occupiers in both cases.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, when a married couple buys an HDB flat, both of them must be listed in the flat application in order to form the core family nucleus.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They also cannot be a mortgagor of the housing loan for the flat.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty (ABSD) was introduced as a cooling measure to moderate investment demand in private residential property and promote a sustainable market.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Broadly speaking, ABSD is applied based on the buyer’s profile and the number of residential properties the buyer owns.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Permanent Residents (PRs) and foreigners will incur ABSD.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As shared previously in this house, the vast majority of married couples buy HDB flats as co-owners.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, a non-resident, married to a Singapore Citizen, cannot be an owner of an HDB flat, and will have to be listed as an essential occupier.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will remain watchful of market trends and adjust our policies where needed, to ensure that the property market remains stable and sustainable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The thrust of my question, the context is in part because of the increasing trend of couples that are getting older before they finally get married.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: As a result, some of these may end up being married with already substantial independent assets, which could include a private property.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: When they get married, if they do not have enough resources to purchase a larger private property, they hope to purchase an HDB, but instead, they are forced to sell off these independent assets that they would have acquired over the course of their professional careers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: So, I am wondering if there is some scope for these kinds of individuals who do get married later, entering the marriage already with significant independent assets, whether there could be some waiver for these kind of MOP requirements.
